- [Jack's Friday workshop update](https://outlook.office365.com/owa/?ItemID=AAMkADVhYjUxODIyLWM5NTktNGJmOC1hN2FjLWFjMjllNWUzYmY4MwBGAAAAAAAEXHdKGOMeRLfpaU7ff8ChBwABLsgQpFdPTayXOZTVrraLAAAAAAEMAAABLsgQpFdPTayXOZTVrraLAAHWswZGAAA%3D&exvsurl=1&viewmodel=ReadMessageItem): S9 (first dev face-to-face) pushed back, as there are no in-person go-lives this side of the year
- CT DESADV call (29 Oct): no Fuse rebuild for now; Ingrid takes folder routing to Edicom — [recording](http://localhost:3000/recordings/20261029-153138-d1e2)
- Matt Shaw is on the invite this time (the 19 Oct action to bring him in); his 2 to 4 Nov leave request starts today

To raise:
- [ ] Peak on-call route and the support-model meeting with Ryan and Dennis (carried ×2)
- [ ] Workshop actions: who owns what, and by when (carried ×2)
- [ ] CT GLN ownership for the Edicom/EDIFACT config: still unowned in ILG (carried ×1)
- [ ] Who from Fuse covers Distraction Duty while Matt is on leave 2 to 4 Nov?

Carried from last time:
- [ ] Harry: Organise a small meeting with Ryan and Dennis on the support model and on-call route
- [ ] Harry: Produce the triage flow chart and runbooks for escalating issues to the Fuse team
- [ ] Harry: Send meeting notes to Jack and Oli
- [ ] Harry: Talk to Testy about moving CT config work to Danny and Steve
- [ ] Jack Bailey: Put together a design for an SFTP-style browser view in Fuse
- [ ] Jack Bailey: Talk to Baron about Fuse representation at the Bifrost operational workshop

tldr: Matt was out, so there was no sprint detail. Harry will set up the support-model call with Ryan today, and Oli offered to be looped in for authority.
Iconic short-ship stays with Jack, who will chase it on the Wednesday call. Oli also wants a clear plan in case it happens again.

Integration status: Flare and the molecules integration are live, with Poland waiting on an operational UPS flow. CT is blocked on Edicom/SAP splitting EDIFACT messages. Jack expects no more go-lives this year.
Snap: Synergy are rolling back the API changes after performance degradation. Load testing is ready, but Harry doubts it is representative until the rollback is done.
Team capacity: the Bifrost team will be about 40% smaller once Harry and Nyla step away, with no short-term cover. Matt is to be read in on strategy and given final say on candidates.
decisions: Jack keeps eyes on the Iconic short-ship issue and raises it on Wednesday's call.
Harry will step back from directing Matt's work but stays informed and remains Matt's manager.
Matt gets final say on the Spectrum candidates.
Harry will handle the Ryan support-model conversation himself and loop Oli in only if he wants extra authority.

actions.text: Set up a call with Ryan (and Dennis) on the support model, going through the runbooks first
Raise the Iconic short-ship issue on Wednesday's call and keep chasing for a resolution
Pick up Jake's Friday note asking for evidence on the Snap performance testing, as part of the catch-up list
Catch up with Jack on the Snap load testing and whether the test instance matches the production software
Tell the Bifrost folk at Wednesday's catch-up that Harry and Nyla are stepping away, and set expectations on the smaller team
Take five minutes with Harry on the TCA file ingestion handover and what Harry does next
Offer to give Matt context on longer-term integration strategy (North Star, Manhattan Scale), once agreed with Harry and Oli

questions: How much should Matt be read in on the long-term integration strategy (North Star, WMS-agnostic work) so soon, and by whom?
Should Snap load testing wait for the API rollback, so it tests the same software?
When and how will the team be told about the new role and the JD, given the North Star readout tomorrow?
How will the Bifrost team be covered while it is 40% smaller, given no short-term capacity and slow compensation changes?
Will CT's Edicom/SAP conversation on splitting EDIFACT message types produce a fix? Nothing has been heard yet.
